bug_semantics: With allow_unsafe_options left at its safe default, a caller can pass a single-character keyword such as n whose value is an option token such as --upload-pack=<attacker command>. The unsafe-option guard examines only the kwarg name (originally n and later reconstructed as -n), so it does not match --upload-pack; Git.transform_kwarg then emits two argv elements, -n and the attacker-controlled --upload-pack value, and Git executes the supplied upload-pack helper. The same name/value disagreement reaches fetch, pull, push, clone/clone_from and, after later guard expansion, ls_remote, iter_commits, blame, and archive.
flaw_origin: e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 introduced the default unsafe-option guards for Remote.fetch, Remote.pull, and Remote.push but passed list(kwargs.keys()) to check_unsafe_options even though the pre-existing transform_kwarg implementation turns a one-character kwarg value into a separate argv token. Commit 5c59e0d63da6180db8a0b349f0ad36fef42aceed later copied the same name-only check into clone/clone_from, and 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 centralized and expanded it as _option_candidates without fixing the value omission; those later changes are propagation/refactoring rather than the first BIC.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object records author Santos Gallegos <stsewd@proton.me> and committer Santos Gallegos <stsewd@proton.me>; its message is only 'Block unsafe options and protocols by default' and has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-r9mr-m37c-5fr3 (referenced by the assigned GHSA-PJJH-F8RP-RJV3/CVE-2026-73625 bundle) states affected <=3.1.53 and patched >=3.1.54, and documents the key-only guard result versus the two-token transform and the --upload-pack command-execution PoC.

git log -L 1068,1078:git/remote.py follows the fetch guard to e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230, where `Git.check_unsafe_options(options=list(kwargs.keys()), ...)` was added, and then to 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738, which merely replaced that expression with `Git._option_candidates([], kwargs)`. This demonstrates that 701ce32 is not the first BIC for the name-only check.

git log -S'options=list(kwargs.keys())' over git/repo/base.py and git/remote.py identifies e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 as the first addition for fetch/pull/push, 5c59e0d63da6180db8a0b349f0ad36fef42aceed as the later clone/clone_from addition, and 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 as the later replacement. git log -S'def _option_candidates' confirms that the centralized collector itself first appears only in 701ce32.

At the BIC, git/remote.py adds unsafe --upload-pack/--receive-pack denylists and default allow_unsafe_options=False checks that inspect only kwargs keys. In the same BIC tree, git/cmd.py transform_kwarg returns [`-<name>`, `<value>`] when len(name)==1 and split_single_char_options is true, proving the guard/executed-argv mismatch from source rather than from later code.

Direct parent-tree verification with `git diff 2625ed9fc074091c531c27ffcba7902771130261 e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 -- git/remote.py git/cmd.py` shows that parent 2625ed9fc074091c531c27ffcba7902771130261 has no default unsafe-option checks in fetch/pull/push; e6108c7 adds the denylists, allow_unsafe_options parameters, and name-only checks. The commit has exactly that one parent, so the guard-bypass state is absent from its immediate parent.

The direct fix e8d0fbf774d1f6baa3b481adfe48bd262e43b453 changes git/cmd.py _option_candidates so that, when one-character options are split, dash-prefixed values are also emitted as unsafe-option candidates; its regression asserts candidates [`-n`, `--upload-pack=helper`] and an UnsafeOptionError. The commit message explicitly references GHSA-r9mr-m37c-5fr3.

`git tag --contains e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 --sort=version:refname` starts at 3.1.30, while 3.1.29 resolves to 19aaa74aafc06663644d634f33bb8af871d58536 before the BIC. Thus the exact default-guard bypass exists from 3.1.30 through 3.1.53; still older releases fall under the advisory's broad <=3.1.53 range because they lacked this default unsafe-option protection rather than bypassing it.

`git tag --contains e8d0fbf774d1f6baa3b481adfe48bd262e43b453` starts at 3.1.54. Tag 3.1.53 resolves to faf3c09038b03bc2bdd8545ef34bbf6d7f1cd11f, which is the fix commit's immediate parent, and tag 3.1.54 resolves to e59d9bab02b095a97e179f47019afee95f4e3c18 with the fix in ancestry, matching the advisory's patched boundary.

reasoning: The dangerous single-character transformation predates the security control, but a guard bypass does not exist until a default guard claims to reject unsafe options and checks a representation different from the argv that will be executed. e6108c7 is the earliest public commit that creates that state: fetch/pull/push inspect kwarg names only, while transform_kwarg emits the value as a second option-capable token. Its immediate parent contains the transform but no such default guard, satisfying parent absence for the vulnerable guard mechanism. The 2023 clone check and the 2026 _option_candidates centralization preserve/expand the same omission and therefore are not smaller introducers; e8d0fbf is the direct repair because it makes the candidate stream include the option-like value. Release ancestry places the guard-bypass lifecycle at 3.1.30 through 3.1.53 and the repair in 3.1.54, while explaining why the advisory's broad lower-unbounded range also covers older unguarded releases. Finally, the e6108c7 commit object is wholly human-attributed and contains no AI marker, so later AI-authored refactors or fixes cannot attribute this BIC and the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
